bio:
Ben helps run PhreakNIC. He is actively managed by his wife, three grown daughters, three cats, and an Alaskan Husky. In his free time he loves being outdoors and has listened to at least one or more audio books a week for 20 years.  His first Phreaknic was 13 and he has served in all the positions of the Nashville2600 at one time or another since 2009. 
He is an Information Security leader for a healthcare company by day and winner of Time Magazine's person of the year in 2006.

name: CrashCart

bio: CrashCart (Tim) likes to resuscitate old computers and game systems when he isn't studying computer science for the fun of it or running developer platforms for the money. A lifelong hacker and maker, he'd hesitate to call himself an "expert," but "consummate amateur" might fit. If you talk to him, tell him what your first computer was.

name: nuvious
topic: Strategies for the Post-LLM Job Market
bio: A veteran of both US Navy, private and public sector Cybersecurity including a background in traditional and LLM AI applications and development. Currently working in FINTECH at a fortune 50 as a Lead Cybersecurity engineer. Academically he is working on a Master's degree in Cybersecurity as a student at Johns Hopkins University studying offensive security and AI applications in Cybersecurity. He's presented at Shmoocon 2025 on a high-entropy covert channel built around the QUIC protocol and got 15 minutes of fame on Hacker New for building a Pluggable Authentication Module that takes covert actions when pre-registered duress passwords are used to login.

name: Elonka
topic: Fact and Fiction of the Knights Templar
bio: Elonka Dunin is an author, cryptographer, and game developer whose public cryptography career began in 2000 when she became the first person to crack the PhreakNIC v3.0 Code. She is the author of The Mammoth Book of Secret Codes and Cryptograms and co-author of Codebreaking: A Practical Guide, now in its second edition (2023). She co-leads the group working on the Kryptos sculpture at CIA Headquarters, and led the international team that cracked Jim Sanborn’s Cyrillic Projector cipher. Dan Brown, author of The Da Vinci Code, named a character in The Lost Symbol after her: “Nola Kaye,” a scrambled version of “Elonka.”
